newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rain falls in some eastern Australian wheat areas.
newsitem.headline: Rain falls in some eastern Australian wheat areas.

text.p: Good rainfalls were recorded in Australia's southeastern wheatgrowing state of Victoria over the weekend after a prolonged dry period which has raised alarm about winter wheat planting prospects.
Reasonably good rain also fell in southern areas of New South Wales (NSW), although rainfall in this state, also affected by the dry, was mostly patchy in wheatgrowing areas.
An official with Victoria's Bureau of Meteorology said on Monday that good falls were recorded across the state.
About 10 millimetres fell across ther Mallee wheat area in Victoria's southwest, he said. The centre of Mildura recorded 0.6 mm on the weekend, the first rainfall there for 82 days, he said.
The central west of the state received 20-25 mm, he said.
"They'd be pretty happy there," the official said.
The northeast of the state, around Albury, received about 10-20 mm.
It was not raining on Monday but more rain might develop on Tuesday, he said.

"Difficult to say yet (if it's looking better generally)," he said. "But that'll certainly help. As long as they get good followup rain and as long as it doesn't cool down too much in the short-term they should get some good growth out of it," he said.
Melbourne had had its driest eight months since 1878/79, while some parts of Victoria have had the driest April on record, he said.

Little significant rain fell over NSW over the weekend, although falls of five to 10 mm were recorded in the south of the state near the Victorian border, an official with the NSW Bureau of Meteorology said.
A few spottings were recorded in many areas across the state, he said.
Sydney has had its driest April since 1896.
